Definition: properly, to adjure, i.e. (usually in a bad sense) imprecate
BiblicalUsage: The word is to adjure — to bind someone by an oath, or to lay a curse. Leviticus makes the man who hears a curse and hides it guilty; Numbers puts the suspected wife under oath; Deuteronomy warns the man who hears the curse of the covenant and blesses himself anyway; and Joshua lays a curse on whoever rebuilds Jericho. Oaths and curses both run on the same word, because both call God to witness.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this word warns me about the weight of words. An oath calls God as witness, a curse calls Him as judge — and the Bible treats both as real, binding, and dangerous. That is why Jesus says to let our yes be yes: a people who speak plainly have no need to swear.
